reasoning: There are 17 pigeons and 16 holes. Since each hole can contain at most one pigeon and each pigeon must be assigned to exactly one hole, it is mathematically impossible to assign all 17 pigeons to the 16 holes. This is a classic example of the pigeonhole principle, which states that if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item. In this case, it is impossible to assign all 17 pigeons to the 16 holes without violating the condition that each hole contains at most one pigeon.
